model_contract.origin: v0.2 prospective coefficients, carried unchanged into PROD v1.0
model_contract.rule: No replay result may alter this contract or the live forecast.

diagnostic_contract.scoreability_gate: stable Democratic/Republican candidate presence at all five fixed checkpoints, frozen before results are opened
diagnostic_contract.rule: Thresholds and scoreability rules are fixed before reviewing diagnostic results and are not model coefficients.

paired_polling_component_test.counterfactual: same race, same checkpoint, same structural + generic-ballot prior, race-level poll blend removed

stages: + admitted race-poll blend / published full forecast

roster_transition_policy.rule: preserve frozen probability; label candidate-pair changes separately in movement diagnostics

baseline_stability.scope: House races with both Democratic and Republican candidates in the admitted fixed sample
baseline_stability.inputs: three already-admitted presidential district margins minus the cycle's frozen national presidential margins
baseline_stability.causal_boundary: Baseline instability may indicate non-stationarity or realignment. It is not a redistricting indicator and must not be interpreted as one without separately admitted boundary-change evidence.

polling_error_decomposition.scope: scoreable races with eligible race-level polls and separately admitted certified D/R two-party result margins
polling_error_decomposition.raw_poll_signal: exact frozen as-of race_poll_average using the production window, candidate matching, quality/sample/sponsor weights and half-life
polling_error_decomposition.causal_boundary: Observed poll error does not by itself identify pollster, sampling, turnout, mode or electorate causes.

source_mix.scope: scoreable races with eligible race-level polls and admitted certified D/R result margins
source_mix.partisan_label_rule: lean D/R counts as partisan-labelled; N or blank is not claimed to be neutral, only not labelled partisan
source_mix.pollster_table_ordering: sample size descending, then name; never error-ranked
source_mix.causal_boundary: Depth, concentration, sponsor labels and pollster identity are observational characteristics of the admitted polling stream, not randomized treatments.

metric_definitions.brier: Mean squared error of Democratic win probability against binary outcome; lower is better.
metric_definitions.log_loss: Mean negative log likelihood; strongly penalises confident errors; lower is better.
metric_definitions.accuracy: Share of races where the side at or above 50% won; secondary to proper scoring rules.
metric_definitions.calibration: Within fixed 10-point probability bins, compares mean forecast probability with observed Democratic win rate.
metric_definitions.calibration_residual: Observed Democratic win rate minus mean forecast probability. Positive means Democratic wins were more frequent than forecast.
metric_definitions.mean_absolute_bin_calibration_error: Count-weighted mean absolute calibration residual across occupied fixed bins.
metric_definitions.calibration_slope_intercept: Logistic recalibration diagnostic; ideal intercept 0 and slope 1. Diagnostic only, never fed back into the model.
metric_definitions.polling_partitions: Conditional performance among races with versus without eligible race-level polls at a checkpoint; not a causal estimate of polling value.
metric_definitions.winner_directed_movement: Probability change signed so positive movement is toward the eventual winner. Outcomes are used only after predictions are frozen.
metric_definitions.scoreability_exclusion: Evaluation-only exclusion decided from predictive roster evidence before outcomes are opened. It changes the scored historical sample, never a forecast probability.
metric_definitions.paired_polling_component_test: For races with eligible race-level polls, compares the published checkpoint probability with that same race's frozen structural + generic-ballot prior before the race-poll blend. Negative Brier/log-loss delta means the race-poll component improved the paired forecasts. Outcomes are used only after both probabilities exist.
metric_definitions.structural_decomposition: On the same two-major-party race sample, scores the admitted structural presidential relative-lean plus incumbency stage, then the structural + generic-ballot prior, then the published full forecast. The structural stage is reconstructed as prior_margin minus the checkpoint generic-ballot margin. Negative deltas mean the later stage improved the same sample.
metric_definitions.roster_transition: A change in the admitted candidate pair between fixed checkpoints. These information-state changes remain in the frozen historical forecast but are labelled separately in movement forensics.
metric_definitions.baseline_stability_range: Range, in percentage points, of the three pre-election presidential relative leans after subtracting each election's frozen national Democratic-minus-Republican margin. Smaller means the structural history was more internally stable.
metric_definitions.poll_margin_error: Estimated Democratic-minus-Republican two-party margin minus certified D-R two-party result margin. Positive values are too Democratic; negative values are too Republican.
metric_definitions.poll_margin_mae: Mean absolute error in percentage points between the exact frozen race-poll aggregate and certified D-R two-party result margin.
metric_definitions.source_concentration: Share of the exact model poll weight contributed by the largest pollster within a race/checkpoint; multi-source races at or above two-thirds are labelled concentrated.
metric_definitions.pollster_race_source: One pollster's weighted aggregate within one race/checkpoint. Repeated polls by the same pollster in the same race count as one race-source observation in pollster tables.

leakage_guards: Corpus state must be explicitly admitted before replay or scoring can run.
Polls are eligible only when publication_date (or end_date if publication_date is absent) is on or before the checkpoint.
Candidate/race roster rows are versioned by known_date; the latest row known by the checkpoint is selected.

The fixed scored sample is frozen before results are opened; races with unstable major-party candidate presence across checkpoints are excluded rather than treating archive missingness as an unopposed race.
Structural presidential baselines must pre-date the cycle and be admitted with provenance.
Election outcome bytes are not opened until every checkpoint prediction and scoreability decision has been produced; outcomes are then passed only to scoring functions.
A checkpoint is not scored if any replayed race lacks an outcome.
Missing generic-ballot input is missing, never zero.
Replay output cannot mutate the live forecast or model contract.
Competitive, polling and chamber diagnostics reuse the frozen checkpoint predictions; they do not create alternative forecasts.
Paired polling-component diagnostics are computed only after the published checkpoint probabilities are frozen; certified outcomes are used solely to score the frozen full and prior probabilities.

Structural-stage diagnostics reconstruct structural+incumbency probability only from already-frozen checkpoint prior_margin and generic-ballot margin; no post-election district or result field enters the predictive stage.

Baseline-stability bands are assigned from admitted presidential structural inputs before certified outcomes are consulted; outcomes are used only to score already-frozen structural and published probabilities within those bands.

Certified result margins are admitted in a separate evaluation-only sidecar and are opened only after checkpoint predictions and the exact as-of poll aggregates are frozen; they cannot enter forecast generation.

Poll-depth, source-count, concentration and partisan-label bands are frozen from predictive poll metadata before certified outcome margins are joined; pollster tables use a fixed minimum of five distinct race-source observations and are never ranked by outcome error.

baseline_stability.interpretation: The stability band is assigned from pre-election variation in the three admitted presidential relative leans on the cycle's own district geography. Outcomes only score frozen probabilities after assignment. High instability can reflect realignment or baseline non-stationarity; it does not by itself identify redistricting as the cause.

scoreability.rule: Race must be present at all fixed checkpoints and retain stable Democratic/Republican candidate presence across them.
scoreability.rationale: An archive that later gains or loses a major-party candidate cannot safely distinguish a true contest-status change from earlier source omission. Missing evidence is not treated as an unopposed race.
